recorded_from_commit_note: CARD-198's implementation, based on main at 3a0b2d1: the commit that replaces the book's packed 6-up/4-up answer key with one full solved page per puzzle (BookPDFGenerator.solved_puzzle_page, CARD-197, reused verbatim). Unlike its predecessors in this chain, this file lands in the SAME commit as the production change (per this card's own pipeline rules), not a following one, so a short hash recorded here would describe a commit that does not exist until this one is made; the branch name is recorded instead. This file is recorded against that commit's own book_corpus.baseline_puzzles(), whose answer section grows from three packed pages (one per level) to four (one per puzzle, since puzzles 2 and 3 share one puzzle page but each still print their own answer page).
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages — the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-198 deliberately changes the interior's answer section: interior pages 9-11, the packed key's three answer pages (one per level), are replaced by four pages 9-12, one full solved page per puzzle in book order (Duck, Owl, Tree, Snowflake), each now also carrying its own clues and revealed fill rather than a packed tile. Pages 1-8 (the guide page, the three level dividers, the two-up page, the two single-puzzle pages and the SOLUTIONS divider) are CARD-184's digests byte for byte (CARD-198 G-2, checked below, not assumed) — only the answer section moved, and it grew by one page.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like as of CARD-198. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, and an interior_bytes that no longer matches means the written file changed. If a later card deliberately changes either, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
interior_colorspace_note: What every page of this interior declares, unaffected by CARD-198 (CARD-147's own fact). NOT the same thing as each page entry's "mode" below, which is "RGB" and always will be: that field is what pdf_pages hands back after its own convert("RGB"), not what the file says.
changed_pages_note: CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: pages 1-8 were compared against book_baseline_card184.json's entries before this file was written, with the font fingerprint reproduced on this machine first, and found byte-identical (CARD-198 G-2, AC-9). Page 12 is new — CARD-184's book had only eleven pages — so "changed" here means "not present in, or not equal to, the predecessor": pages 9-11 moved in place and page 12 is an addition.
font_fingerprint_note: Unchanged from CARD-149/184's value, reproduced on this machine before this file was written. The guide page still letters its title at 92 px and its body at 46 px, and the divider at type_px(DIVIDER_PT, 300) = 60 px. The answer pages' band and caption letter in the packaged DejaVu Sans (solved_puzzle_page, CARD-197), which does not depend on the machine.
font_dependent_pages_note: Unchanged from CARD-147: page 1 is the guide page (Arial, with the load_default fallback), pages 2, 4, 6 and 8 the dividers. None of the four new-shape answer pages (9-12) are machine-lettered.
interior_bytes_note: The black-and-white interior of this book: 2,981,925 bytes where CARD-184 recorded 2,437,097 for an eleven-page book. The difference is pages 9-12's own JPEG streams: pages 1-8 contribute the same bytes they always did (CARD-198 G-2).
colour_interior_bytes_note: The same book with a COLOUR interior: 3,443,143 bytes where CARD-184 recorded 2,845,507 for the eleven-page book. Read by tests/test_book_pdf_ink_mode.py only to show the length moved (TestBookInk_ColourInteriorIsUnchanged), not to pin a new one — no CARD-198 colour-specific fixture is recorded (out of this card's Touches); see that test module's own CARD-198 note.
